```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The `rddinterf` package estimates effects in a sharp regression discontinuity
design when each unit's outcome may depend on its neighbors' treatments. It uses
the distance to an effective-treatment boundary as the running variable and
allows the variance to reflect dependence through a supplied graph.

## Inputs

The main function requires:

- `Yi`: the observed outcome vector;
- `Xi`: the individual running variable;
- `neighbors`: a list whose `i`th element contains the observation indices of
  unit `i`'s neighbors;
- `W`: the dependency graph, with rows and columns ordered like `Yi`;
- `contrasts`: a named list of effective-treatment contrasts; and
- `exposure`: the neighborhood exposure mapping.

Each contrast has the form `list(c(d, g), c(dprime, gprime))`. The first pair
is placed on the right of the distance cutoff and the second on the left.

## Example

The following small ring network illustrates the required data structures.

```{r}
library(rddinterf)

set.seed(123)
n <- 80
Xi <- runif(n, -1, 1)
neighbors <- lapply(seq_len(n), function(i) {
  c(if (i == 1) n else i - 1L, if (i == n) 1L else i + 1L)
})

W <- diag(n)
for (i in seq_len(n)) W[i, neighbors[[i]]] <- 1
W <- (W + t(W) > 0) * 1

Di <- as.integer(Xi >= 0)
Gi <- as.numeric(vapply(neighbors, function(j) any(Di[j] == 1), logical(1)))
Yi <- 1 + Di + 0.3 * Gi + 0.5 * Xi + rnorm(n, sd = 0.2)

contrasts <- list(
  direct = list(c(1, 0), c(0, 0)),
  spillover = list(c(0, 1), c(0, 0))
)

fit <- rddinterf(
  Yi, Xi, neighbors, W, contrasts,
  exposure = "one.treated",
  estimator = "conventional",
  h = 0.8,
  b = 1
)

fit
```

`ov_direct` is the discontinuity in the individual running variable and
`ov_indirect` is the discontinuity in the nearest neighbor score. The remaining
rows correspond to the named contrasts supplied in `contrasts`. Use
`summary(fit)` to obtain the underlying numeric summary matrix.

## Exposure mappings

Four mappings are available:

- `"one.treated"`: whether at least one neighbor is treated;
- `"sum.treated"`: the number of treated neighbors;
- `"frac.treated"`: the fraction of treated neighbors; and
- `"majority"`: whether at least half of the neighbors are treated.

Use `estimator = "conventional"` for the conventional local polynomial
estimator or `estimator = "robust"` for bias-corrected estimation and robust
inference. Bandwidths are selected automatically unless `h` and `b` are
supplied.

## Neighborhood strata with different codimensions

The convergence rate depends on the codimension of the effective-treatment
boundary. If a contrast pools neighborhood strata with different codimensions,
`rddinterf()` reports a warning. As established in the paper, such a pooled
estimator converges to a weighted average of boundary effects over the strata
with minimum codimension. To target effects in every stratum, estimate the
stratum-specific effects separately and aggregate them with the appropriate
density weights.
